# 120.00 USD parked in a USD account, against a 100.00 USD invoice.
#
# The single-currency shape, which is the common one: bank,
# `Assets:Suspense USD`, receivable and invoice are all USD, so nothing
# converts and the entry is USD throughout. The figure on the
# `Assets:Suspense USD` split *is* what the bank received — unlike the
# cross-currency fixtures beside it, where `Assets:Due From Director` carries
# 166.80 CAD that is an artefact of that account's own currency.
#
# It is 20.00 more than the invoice owes, so linking it is an overpayment and
# the file has to say what the residue is. Nothing about the currencies makes
# that question go away.
#
# What this fixture produces: a USD transaction, bank +120 against suspense
# −120, neither split in a lot.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
2026-03-02 * "Money in, USD suspense, too much"
	guid: "1928374655647382910abcdef0123456"
	currency.mnemonic: "USD"
	Assets:Bank:USD 120.00 USD
		guid: "28374655647382910abcdef012345671"
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
	Assets:Suspense USD -120.00 USD
		guid: "37465564738291a0bcdef012345678ab"
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
